Subject: Throughput guarantees & GPU selection for Nimbus Analytics dedicated pool

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Nimbus is very interested in a Redwood Dedicated pool for our production inference. Before we lock a commit, procurement asked for a short write-up on the tradeoffs between H100 / A100 / L40S for our workload so they can justify the spend. A few details on our side:~
- Peak concurrent requests: ~400 qps during business hours (US PST) with heavy short-chat traffic and ~10% long-context summarization jobs (~8k tokens).
- Latency target: p95 < 250ms for chat flows; batching allowed for bulk scoring jobs.
- Preferred retention: 12 month commit preferred but open to 3/6 month pilots.
- Memory requirement: some models need >40GB activation memory for long-context.

Could you provide: a) a throughput / perf-per-dollar comparison across H100/A100/L40S for this mix, b) recommended commit sizing (GPU count + tier) to hit our p95 SLO, and c) example pricing for 3m vs 12m reserved commits?

If easier, we can hop on a 30 minute call today. Procurement is awaiting the note to move the PO flow.

Thanks,
Laura

Subject: Internal: Nimbus perf/$ analysis (H100 vs A100 vs L40S)

Internal note — do not forward without redaction. Below are the high-level assumptions and recommended packaging we should surface to Nimbus. Numbers are approximate and tuned to their workload description.

Summary of hardware tradeoffs (short):
- H100 (80GB variant): best single-card latency and throughput for transformer workloads that benefit from sparse kernels and bf16/fp16 fused ops. Highest perf per card, but also highest unit price. Best for low p95 latency and long-context models.
- A100 (40/80GB): strong general-purpose; better than L40S for very large activations (80GB variant), lower raw attention throughput vs H100 on newer kernels; mid-tier cost.
- L40S (48GB-ish inference-card): optimized for inference density and lower cost; great perf/$ for batched scoring and embeddings, but less headroom for very long sequences and slightly worse p95 latency under tight SLOs.

Perf/$ proxy (relative, normalized to H100 = 1.0 perf):
- H100: perf 1.00, unit rate 1.00 (baseline high cost)
- A100: perf ~0.78, unit rate ~0.72 (good for memory-bound long-context)
- L40S: perf ~0.62, unit rate ~0.45 (best perf/$ for bulk scoring)

Implications for Nimbus:
- Given p95 < 250ms requirement and 10% long-context jobs, a mixed fleet is ideal: H100s to absorb latency-critical chat traffic and long-context summarization; L40S to handle the bulk of batched scoring/embeddings.

Suggested committed packaging (three options):
1) Latency-first (SLO focus): 8 x H100 reserved, target utilization 55-70%. Expect p95 ~ 140-220ms depending on batching behavior. 12-month commit recommended for best per-hour rate.
2) Balanced (recommended): 4 x H100 + 12 x L40S. Put H100s behind a low-latency route (canary for chat); L40S pool for bulk and overflow. Expected blended perf/$ improvement ~18-25% vs H100-only. 12-month commit, optionally with 3-month pilot (smaller commit) and ramp to 12m within quarter.
3) Throughput-first (cost focus): 18 x L40S. Lower p95 risk — add autoscaling buffers or low-latency fallback to hosted route to protect chat SLO. Best raw perf/$ for heavy batched workloads.

Commit sizing guidance: recommend we convert expected qps -> tokens/sec and run a short synthetic of their model family, but ballpark: for their 400 qps peak with 10% long-context, Balanced option should provide ~20-30% headroom. If procurement will only ok 3 months, price with higher unit rate and include a migration credit if they convert to 12 months within 90 days.

Pricing levers to include in the proposal:
- Commit length (3m vs 12m): 12m gives ~12-18% lower GPU-hour rate.
- Utilization floors: guarantee 45-60% utilization bands to give deeper discounts at higher committed floors.
- Mixed-fleet discount: blended discounts if they commit to H100 + L40S in the same deal (we can offer a cross-fleet credit).

Risks / callouts:
- Long-context memory needs may force A100 (80GB) in edge cases; confirm largest activation size (we should ask for a sample model/trace).
- If they need strict p99 SLOs for chat, we should price for additional reserved H100 headroom.

I'll prepare a condensed memo we can send to Laura + procurement with the recommended Balanced option and an explicit 3m vs 12m price delta.

S — Soojin
Soojin Lee

Hi Laura / Procurement team — following up with a concise proposal based on the internal analysis. See attached: Redwood_Dedicated_Terms_v2.pdf and the cost matrix we discussed. Key recommendation (balanced option):

- Configuration: 4 x H100 (low-latency route) + 12 x L40S (throughput route)
- Expected SLO: p95 chat latency target < 250ms with ~25% headroom; batch scoring throughput comfortably absorbed by L40S pool.
- Commit options: 3-month pilot (pro-rated higher unit rate) or 12-month reserved commit. Example pricing delta: ~15% lower blended GPU-hour rate for 12m vs 3m. Exact numbers are in the spreadsheet.
- Commercials: Deal ID DEAL-9831; if you sign a 12m commit within 30 days we can offer an additional one-time onboarding credit (covers first-month overage) and a migration credit if you move more workloads from hosted to dedicated within 90 days.

Next steps: please confirm which commit term you prefer (3m pilot vs 12m) and whether you want a short call tomorrow to walk the spreadsheet before procurement raises the PO. If helpful, we can include a clause for an interim autoscaling buffer for the first 30 days to handle surge risk.

Thanks,
